outcome: Alerts from tools already owned are correlated into a single incident view, so analysts stop guessing how separate detections relate.
overview: Most enterprises already own more detection sources than they correlate: an endpoint tool, a firewall, an email gateway, an identity platform, each alerting into its own console. Cisco XDR is aimed at that specific situation — it correlates across sources, including third-party ones, rather than requiring the estate to be replaced first. Whether it helps depends almost entirely on which of the existing sources can be integrated with useful fidelity, which is an assessment question and not a product one.

benefits.text: Detections from several existing tools are correlated into one incident view
benefits.limits: Correlation fidelity varies sharply by integration; a source that contributes only alerts, without underlying telemetry, adds little

benefits.text: The existing tool estate is reused rather than replaced as a precondition
benefits.limits: Reuse avoids a replacement programme; it does not improve a source whose own detection quality is the actual problem

benefits.text: Threat intelligence is applied consistently across the correlated sources
benefits.limits: Intelligence improves prioritisation, not coverage; a technique nobody collects telemetry for stays invisible however good the intelligence is

residency: Cloud-delivered correlation; detection metadata leaves the customer estate and the tenant region is recorded at design

notFor.situation: An estate with one detection source and no plan for more
notFor.why: There is nothing to correlate across, and a correlation layer over a single source is overhead

notFor.situation: A team already running a correlation platform with tuned content
notFor.why: The accumulated content does not port, and a second correlation layer produces two incident queues

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco security implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to the agreed sources integrated with triage moved to the correlated queue
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed correlation tuning.
1) Assess — source inventory, per-source integration fidelity, investigation-time baseline
2) Design — integration map, correlation expectations per source pair, triage migration plan
3) Integrate — sources connected at their assessed fidelity, correlation validated
4) Migrate and hand over — triage moved to the correlated queue, operations handed over
deliverables: The fidelity achieved per source is documented and matches the assessment
A correlated incident demonstrably relates detections from at least two sources
Analysts work the correlated queue rather than the per-tool queues
effort: 8–12 weeks to the agreed sources integrated with triage moved to the correlated queue
languages: English delivery; Arabic executive materials on request
